constraints: Use AssetComposition, AssetInstance, AssetBinding, exact definition versions, and immutable SystemBuilderRevision snapshots; do not create a renderer-only or parallel graph model.
Represent containment separately from data, event, control, resource, runtime, adapter, and dependency bindings.
Every new interactive system has exactly one protected System Foundation-derived root and a required application shell/page host; non-interactive profiles remain possible.
Provide only versioned predefined application-shell and page-layout presets; users do not create slots, enter CSS, or choose raw dimensions.
Do not mutate system.foundation@1.0.0 or historical system revisions; introduce additive versions and explicit upgrade revisions.
Keep desktop and thin client on the same shared UI and transport semantics with explicit workspace scope and optimistic conflict handling.
Generate instance controls from safe effective definition schemas and UI hints; keep raw JSON as an advanced fallback only.
Preserve a complete native-control/keyboard path and semantic source order; pointer drag and drop cannot be the only editing mechanism.
Preview remains side-effect-free and cannot execute imported/authored implementation or backend code without a separately qualified sandbox.
Preserve the current uncommitted Compose preview changes as baseline work outside this successor roadmap.

discovery.summary: System Builder currently saves a flat ordered instance list, promotes the first instance to root, and edits selectedConfiguration as raw JSON. Asset Kernel definitions already provide configuration schemas, UI hints, ports, composition rules, and immutable revisions, but they do not provide parent-instance placement or named slot vocabulary. System Foundation exposes containers, pages, navigation groups, and a System Shell, yet the System Shell does not admit an application-shell/page hierarchy. The existing Increment 5 roadmap claims hierarchy and schema-backed inspection that the implemented UI does not provide.

risks: The Asset Library detail DTO intentionally exposes summaries, not canonical schemas or ports; the composer needs its own bounded application read model rather than renderer reconstruction or N+1 detail calls.

Pointer drag-and-drop alone would exclude keyboard users and make test behavior fragile; explicit add, move, reparent, reorder, wrap, and remove controls are canonical while pointer interactions remain progressive enhancement.
Undo/redo must snapshot only the local draft and must not bypass optimistic save conflicts or create hidden persistence writes.
Generated controls must preserve all supported JSON value kinds, constraints, section ordering, and invalid draft feedback without silently applying schema defaults.
Recursive preview must be bounded and render only trusted declarative Foundation surfaces; it cannot execute imported or authored frontend/backend logic.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The Manage tab lists every system visible to the active workspace exactly once across drafted and published lifecycle states, exposes truthful current-revision and update metadata, and supports bounded search, status filtering, sorting, refresh, and usable loading, empty, and error states.

A user can preview an eligible drafted or published system from Manage using the canonical bounded recursive preview and can open the selected system in Compose without losing its exact revision, hierarchy, configuration, or publication state.

Deletion is available only when the application-owned policy marks a system eligible, always identifies the exact target and consequence in a confirmation dialog, detects stale or conflicting state, preserves immutable retained history required by policy, and refreshes the list after success without renderer-local mutation truth.

Every displayed lifecycle action is derived from canonical state and either succeeds through the established use case and transport boundary or remains visibly unavailable with a useful reason; failures are bounded, redacted, and leave the list and selected system consistent.

The shared Manage experience is keyboard operable, uses accessible list/table and dialog semantics, reflows without unintended page overflow, restores focus after preview and confirmation dialogs, and passes desktop and thin-client transport, build, and interaction parity checks.

plan.summary: Deliver Increment 3 in two cohesive vertical chunks: first an application-owned lifecycle projection carried through both host transports and clients, then a complete shared Manage experience with responsive discovery, truthful publication state, recursive preview, Compose handoff, and guarded delete/archive/restore actions. Focused checks run per chunk; full gates run once after the increment is complete.

risks: Treating validated as published would conflate design-time readiness with an approved immutable release and mislabel systems; publication must be derived from exact release records.

Physically deleting records or revisions would break immutable history and published build/release references; Delete must be an explicit archive transition unless a later retention/purge decision is approved.
Joining system and release data in React would duplicate policy and drift between desktop and thin client; the application projection must own publication and action eligibility.
Opening Compose from Manage requires controlled top-level tab state and an explicit initial system selection; renderer-global state or URL invention is unnecessary.
Preview must resolve the exact current revision and bounded composer catalog, report unsupported surfaces, and retain the existing non-execution boundary.
Dense action controls can create long keyboard sequences; native table/list semantics, concise row actions, confirmation focus restoration, and responsive reflow need focused interaction tests.

research.summary: System Builder already owns workspace-scoped records, immutable revisions, optimistic archive/restore, and separate immutable build releases. Design-time status intentionally does not mean published, so Manage needs an application-owned bounded projection joining records to releases. The safe deletion behavior is the existing archive transition presented transparently as removal from active systems: it retains revisions/releases, detects stale revisions, and supports restoration. The shared TabbedPanel already supports controlled navigation, ModalDialog owns focus containment/restoration, and the recursive preview can be reused without executing unqualified code. A native semantic table at wide widths with a reflowed list/card presentation at narrow widths preserves understandable reading order and native control behavior.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every supported historical flat revision remains byte-for-byte immutable and readable; upgrading creates a reviewed new slot-aware revision, preserves every compatible instance/configuration/binding, places unmatched content in an explicit unassigned state, and supports cancel/retry/conflict without data loss.

Secured data-entry, controlled chatbot, and secured data-review templates materialize exact Foundation-derived roots, appropriate application/page presets, valid placements and typed bindings, recursively preview their UI, and preserve their existing security and Run and Test behavior.

Build and release inputs freeze exact slot, placement, layout-definition, instance-configuration, backing-resource, and binding data; equivalent revisions reproduce identical content digests, meaningful hierarchy changes alter them, and tampering or missing exact definitions fails closed before approval or deployment.

Maximum instance, placement, depth, slot-child, configuration, binding, diagnostic, and rendered-node limits prevent excessive work; malformed, cyclic, cross-workspace, unsafe, stale, revoked, or unsupported inputs return bounded redacted errors and never widen code, secret, filesystem, network, build, release, or runtime authority.
Live PostgreSQL qualification proves the same slot-aware revision, conflict, workspace-isolation, legacy-read, upgrade, and immutable-history semantics as SQLite/structured local persistence.

A packaged Windows desktop application and supported thin-client browser each complete create, choose layout, nest, configure, connect, preview, save, reopen, switch layout, upgrade legacy, build, manage, and inspect revision history against their real IPC/API paths.

Controlled keyboard and assistive-technology review confirms understandable tree/canvas/inspector/manage navigation and focus behavior; every approved preset satisfies WCAG 2.2 reflow expectations at 320 CSS pixels or equivalent zoom, preserves semantic reading order, and passes reviewed desktop/tablet/mobile visual baselines in light and dark themes.

Representative bounded-scale compositions and system lists remain responsive within documented targets, interrupted/conflicting saves, failed upgrades, and guarded lifecycle actions recover without revision loss, rollback disables new activation without flattening slot-aware data, and operator/contributor documentation states supported and unsupported behavior truthfully.
